evidence.quote: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MISSISSIPPI

summary.short: Makes it a crime to knowingly disseminate a non-consensual deepfake ('digitization') of a person within 90 days of an election, intending to injure a candidate, influence results or deter voting. Penalties up to 1 year or $5,000, or up to 5 years or $10,000. Effective July 1, 2024.
summary.long: The act adds a section to Title 97, Chapter 13 of the Mississippi Code. Section 1(1) defines 'candidate', 'digitization' (altered or computer-generated images or audio, including those made with software or machine learning artificial intelligence, that a reasonable person would believe depict conduct the depicted individual did not engage in), 'depicted individual' and 'disseminates'. Section 1(2) makes it a crime to disseminate, or contract to disseminate, a digitization with knowledge that it is one, if it is disseminated within 90 days of an election, without the depicted individual's consent, and with intent to injure a candidate, influence the results of an election or deter voting. Section 1(3) sets penalties: up to 5 years or a fine up to $10,000, or both, where there is intent to incite violence, cause bodily harm or deter voting, or a prior conviction within 5 years; otherwise up to 1 year or a fine up to $5,000, or both. Section 1(4) allows injunctive relief against a person reasonably believed to be about to violate or violating the section, sought by the Attorney General, a district attorney, the depicted individual, an injured candidate, or an injured political party whose nominee is on the ballot; the court may order removal of disseminated digitizations. Section 1(5) makes clear and prominent on-screen disclaimers that the depicted individual did not engage in the depicted conduct a defense to prosecution. Section 1(6) excludes interactive computer and information service providers, broadcasters in bona fide news coverage or paid broadcasts, certain news publishers that clearly state content does not accurately represent a ballot issue or candidate, satire or parody, and security, fraud or investigative uses. Section 2 sets the effective date as July 1, 2024.

relations.note: Section 1(6)(a) exempts providers of an interactive computer service as defined in 47 USC 230(f) from the section.
Section 1(6)(a) exempts providers of an information service or communications service as defined in 47 USC 153 from the section.

notes: Short-form annotation. The text sets criminal penalties in Section 1(3) but names no prosecuting authority. Section 1(6)(d) uses the terms election communication and materially deceptive media, which are not defined in Section 1(1). Section 1(6)(c) exempts stations or platforms that are paid to broadcast a digitization, as written. Section 1(4) grants injunctive-relief actions to named parties; no damages action is stated. The Code section number is not given. Effective date is July 1, 2024 (Section 2).

"Candidate" means an individual who seeks a nomination or election to a federal, statewide, state district, legislative, judicial, county, county district or municipal office.

"Digitization" means to alter an image or audio in a realistic manner utilizing an image or audio of a person, other than the person depicted, computer-generated images or audio, commonly called deepfakes.
"Depicted individual" means an individual in a digitization who appears to be engaging in speech and/or conduct.
"Disseminates" means transmitting a digitization to another person through social media, electronic mail, electronic messaging, video-sharing services or any other physical or electronic method.
an interactive computer service, as defined in 47 USC Section 230(f)
an information service or communications service, as defined in 47 USC Section 153

obligations.summary: Prohibits a person from disseminating, or contracting or agreeing to disseminate, a digitization (deepfake) that the person knows is a digitization, where the dissemination occurs within 90 days of an election, is made without the depicted individual's consent, and is made with intent to injure a candidate, influence election results or deter voting. Violation is a crime under subsection (3). Exemptions in subsection (6) and the defence in subsection (5) are not recorded as obligations.
obligations.conditional_on: Knowledge that the item is a digitization; dissemination within ninety (90) days of an election; no consent of the depicted individual; intent to injure a candidate, influence election results or deter voting.
